shared_elements: low-relief carving on weathered stone surface
incised linear elements (long lines / arcs) crossing the field
raised flat-topped relief with plain background
justification: Both surfaces carry shallow, flat-topped relief figures reserved against a plain pecked ground, and in each case an animal is rendered as a profile silhouette with simple stick-like limbs, alongside long incised lines that structure the field. The decisive difference is composition: A shows a single isolated creature with a couple of sweeping incised arcs on an otherwise empty pillar face, whereas B is a densely packed multi-register panel with a row of repeated arc motifs above a banded divider and several figures below.
